text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Activities of private security firms are to be closely monitored as part of measures to tighten internal security following the recent wave of bomb explosions in Nigeria.

- Prospects of military intervention by West African nations in Sierra Leone to flush out soldiers who seized power in a coup heightens as Commonwealth secretary general Emeka Anyaoku justifies foreign intervention in the crisis.
- State oil firm Nigerian National Petroleum Corporation defies directive of finance minister that all government property should be insured with state insurer NICON.
- Guilty verdict on armed robbery suspects in eastern Owerri town averts riot by crowd which kept vigil at court premises on Friday as judgment in the celebrated case was read.
- Pastor Alexander Baba, supreme head of Celestial Church of Christ worldwide has been flown to Germany with kidney ailment.

- Northern elders forum, a leading political pressure group, has urged military ruler General Sani Abacha to delay his planned hand over to a democratically elected president by two years to 2000 from 1998 in order to ensure true reconciliation.
- One year after the murder of Kudirat Abiola, senior wife of detained presidential claimant Moshood Abiola, police vow to find the killers.
- Fuel shortage cripples business in northern Kano city.
